subject: Operational handbook: exit rights, notice windows & termination-for-convenience
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@acme-cloud.com>, procurement@acme-cloud.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational handbook: exit rights, notice windows & termination-for-convenience

Tom / Acme procurement — thanks again for the productive call this morning. Attached is the redline we've been iterating on (ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx). The main points we want to align on for the order form / MSA:

- Auto-renew mechanics: proposed 12-month initial term with annual auto-renew unless either party provides 60 days' written notice prior to renewal.
- Notice windows & effective dates: prefer notice to be tied to billing cycle (30/60/90 days) — proposal attached shows 60 days.
- Termination for convenience (T4C): Redwood is willing to include a limited T4C right on the order form with a 90-day notice and pro-rated termination liability limited to remaining pre-paid but non-refundable services.

We expect Acme Legal to push back on the language around "pro-rated" vs "liquidated damages" and whether convenience termination can be exercised in the middle of a committed capacity period. If useful, I've flagged the concession matrix in the summary spreadsheet (redline-summary.xlsx).

Next steps I propose: 
1) Acme legal provides annotated redline (we can accept comments in Word).
2) Redwood legal (Laura) to propose one clean fallback alternative for T4C and a short paragraph explaining the operational impact (billing & data handoff).
3) If redlines are narrow, run for internal exec approval and DocuSign. If more substantive, schedule a 30-minute legal sync.

Please confirm if 60 days for auto-renew is acceptable from Acme's perspective or if procurement needs 30 days to align with your PO processing.

Attachment: ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx (Word redline)
Attachment: redline-summary.xlsx (xls)

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

[Attachment: ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx (40KB)]
[Attachment: redline-summary.xlsx (12KB)]

From: Sarah Li <sli@acme-cloud.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement@acme-cloud.com
Cc: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 17:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational handbook: exit rights, notice windows & termination-for-convenience

Ben — thanks for sending. Attached are Acme's comments (inline in Word) and a short note from procurement: we cannot accept a T4C that allows termination without some measure to recoup onboarding costs for reserved capacity. Specific asks: 

1) If Redwood insists on a 90-day T4C, Acme requests a 6-month minimum notice for capacity-committed line items (or payment of unused committed capacity).
2) Auto-renew window: procurement prefers 30 days so our finance team has time to raise a PO.
3) Liquidated damages: Acme won't accept open-ended "liability limited to pre-paid services" language; propose either (a) a capped termination fee equal to 50% of remaining committed fees, or (b) a mutual termination-for-convenience with proportional refund calculations.

We added inline comments where the redline references "committed pool" and how billing credits would be returned. Also flagged data-handling obligations on termination (handoff timeframe, export format).

Attaching: ACME_MSA_comments_v1.docx

--
Sarah Li
Senior Counsel, Acme Cloud Solutions
sli@acme-cloud.com

[Attachment: ACME_MSA_comments_v1.docx (28KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational handbook: exit rights, notice windows & termination-for-convenience

Team — I reviewed Acme's comments and sketched two paths we can present: 

OPTION A (commercial compromise — faster):
- Keep 60-day auto-renew but agree to a 30-day procurement notification offset (i.e., Acme must notify 60 days before renewal, but Redwood will accept PO within 30 days after notice to accommodate finance).
- For T4C: allow termination with 90 days' notice but add a capped termination fee equal to the lesser of (a) 50% of remaining committed fees, or (b) the value of 6 months of committed capacity. This addresses Acme's concern on recouping onboarding while limiting Redwood's exposure.
- Commit to a 30-day data export window with standard export format and one complimentary assisted export.

OPTION B (legal-conservative — slower):
- Mutual T4C only (both parties can terminate) with a proportional refund calculation for pre-paid amounts and an elevated notice for capacity-committed SKUs (180 days).
- No capped fee; keep liability carveouts but provide an explicit onboarding cost schedule to be appended to the order form.

Recommendation: start with OPTION A in written response to Acme (faster commercial path). I'll draft the fallback language to insert into the Word redline and attach an explanation paragraph for the commercial team to share. If Acme pushes back on the cap number, we can escalate for exec approval.

I've attached a short patch (redline fragment) you can send back to Acme: ACME_redline_patch_OPTIONA.docx

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal Operations — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0199

[Attachment: ACME_redline_patch_OPTIONA.docx (6KB)]

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational handbook: exit rights, notice windows & termination-for-convenience

Tom / Sarah / Procurement team — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear asks. Per Laura's note, Redwood is prepared to move with OPTION A as the commercial baseline:

- Auto-renew: Redwood will accept 60-day notice but will include a 30-day PO grace period for Acme's finance team as described. Please confirm PO timing expectation.
- T4C: Redwood will accept a limited termination-for-convenience with a capped termination fee (the lesser of 50% of remaining committed fees or 6 months' committed capacity), and a 90-day notice window. For capacity-line items that are pre-paid/committed, we will add a short onboarding cost schedule to the order form as a separate exhibit.
- Data: 30-day export with one assisted export included; longer assisted exports can be quoted as professional services.

If that direction works, Laura will issue the short patch and we can get a DocuSign envelope out next week. If you need the capped fee number adjusted, flag which of the two cap metrics you prefer and we'll surface to execs.

Proposed next steps:
1) Acme to confirm acceptance of OPTION A in reply.
2) Redwood to issue DocuSign link with patched order form (target: send by 2026-05-20).
3) Procurement to confirm PO timelines.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Best,

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
